items.stem: In the given figure, PA and PB are tangents from external point P to a circle with centre C and Q is any point on the circle. Then the measure of ∠AQB is
items.answer: The radii CA and CB are perpendicular to the tangents PA and PB, so in quadrilateral PACB the angle at the centre and the angle at P are supplementary: ∠ACB + ∠APB = 180°, giving ∠ACB = 180° − 55° = 125°. The angle subtended by the chord AB at the centre is twice the angle it subtends at any point Q on the remaining arc, so ∠AQB = ½ × 125° = 62½°.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: From an external point Q, the length of tangent to a circle is 12 cm and the distance of Q from the centre of circle is 13 cm. The radius of circle (in cm) is
items.answer: The radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent PQ at the point of contact, so triangle OPQ is right angled at P. By Pythagoras, OP² = OQ² − PQ² = 13² − 12² = 169 − 144 = 25, hence OP = 5 cm.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: QP is a tangent to a circle with centre O at a point P on the circle. If ΔOPQ is isosceles, then ∠OQR equals.
items.answer: The radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent QP at P, so ∠OPQ = 90°. Since ΔOPQ is isosceles, the two angles other than the right angle are equal, so ∠POQ = ∠OQP. From the angle sum, 2∠OQP + 90° = 180°, giving ∠OQP = 45°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius
items.ocr: The stem as printed asks for ∠OQR, but no point R appears in the question or in the printed figure; the worked solution finds ∠OQP = 45°, which matches key (b). Treated as a misprint for ∠OQP.

items.stem: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm, subtends a right angle at its centre. The length of the chord (in cm) is
items.answer: Let the chord be BC and the centre A, so AB = AC = 10 cm and ∠BAC = 90°. By Pythagoras, BC² = AB² + AC² = 10² + 10² = 200, hence BC = 10√2 cm.
items.concept: Secant of a circle

items.stem: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at E such that AE = 2.4 cm, BE = 3.2 cm and CE = 1.6 cm. The length of DE is
items.answer: For two chords intersecting inside a circle, AE × EB = CE × ED. Substituting, 2.4 × 3.2 = 1.6 × ED, so ED = 7.68 ÷ 1.6 = 4.8 cm.
items.concept: Secant of a circle

items.stem: In figure, O is the centre of circle. PQ is a chord and PT is tangent at P which makes an angle of 50° with PQ. ∠POQ is
items.answer: The radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent PT, so ∠OPT = 90°. Hence ∠OPQ = 90° − 50° = 40°. Since OP = OQ are radii, triangle OPQ is isosceles and ∠OQP = ∠OPQ = 40°. Therefore ∠POQ = 180° − 40° − 40° = 100°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In figure, AP, AQ and BC are tangents of the circle with centre O. If AB = 5 cm, AC = 6 cm and BC = 4 cm, then the length of AP (in cm) is
items.answer: Tangents drawn from an external point are equal, so BP = BR, CR = CQ and AP = AQ, where R is the point at which BC touches the circle. The perimeter of ΔABC is AB + BC + AC = AB + BR + RC + AC = AB + BP + CQ + AC = AP + AQ = 2AP. Hence 5 + 4 + 6 = 2AP, so AP = 15/2 = 7.5 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: If a regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius r, then its perimeter is
items.answer: A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle splits into six equilateral triangles with the centre, so each side equals the radius r. The perimeter is therefore 6 × r = 6r.
items.concept: Secant of a circle

items.stem: In figure, on a circle of radius 7 cm, tangent PT is drawn from a point P such that PT = 24 cm. If O is the centre of the circle, then the length of PR is
items.answer: The tangent PT is perpendicular to the radius OT, so in right triangle PTO, OP² = OT² + PT² = 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625, giving OP = 25 cm. Since OR is a radius, OR = 7 cm, and PR = OP + OR = 25 + 7 = 32 cm.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: Two circles of radii 20 cm and 37 cm intersect in A and B. If O₁ and O₂ are their centres and AB = 24 cm, then the distance O₁O₂ is equal to
items.answer: The line of centres bisects the common chord AB at right angles at C, so AC = 12 cm. In the right triangles, CO₁ = √(37² − 12²) = √(1369 − 144) = 35 cm and CO₂ = √(20² − 12²) = √(400 − 144) = 16 cm. Hence O₁O₂ = 35 + 16 = 51 cm.
items.concept: Secant of a circle

items.stem: In the adjoining figure, TP and TQ are the two tangents to a circle with centre O. If ∠POQ = 110°, then ∠PTQ is
items.answer: The radii OP and OQ are perpendicular to the tangents TP and TQ, so ∠OPT = ∠OQT = 90°. In quadrilateral OPTQ the four angles sum to 360°, so 110° + 90° + ∠PTQ + 90° = 360°, giving ∠PTQ = 70°.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: AB and CD are two common tangents to circles which touch each other at a point C. If D lies on AB such that CD = 4 cm then AB is
items.answer: D is the external point from which DA and DC are tangents to the first circle, so AD = CD; likewise DB and DC are tangents to the second circle, so BD = CD. Hence AB = AD + BD = 2CD = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: In the adjoining figure, PT is a tangent at point C of the circle. O is the circumference of ΔABC. If ∠ACP = 118°, then the measure of ∠x is
items.answer: Join OC. Since OC is a radius and PT is the tangent at C, ∠OCP = 90°. Given ∠ACP = 118°, so ∠ACO = 118° − 90° = 28°. As O is the circumcentre, OA = OC, making triangle OAC isosceles, so ∠OAC = ∠ACO. Hence x = 28°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius
items.ocr: The stem prints 'O is the circumference of ΔABC'; the solution and the figure both treat O as the circumcentre. Printed wording kept.

items.stem: Two concentric circles of radii a and b where a > b, The length of a chord of the larger circle which touches the other circle is
items.answer: Let the chord AB of the larger circle touch the smaller circle at L. Then OL ⊥ AB with OL = b and OA = a. In right triangle OAL, AL = √(a² − b²). The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so AB = 2AL = 2√(a² − b²).
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In the given figure, a circle touches all the four sides of quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 6 cm, BC = 7 cm and CD = 4 cm, then length of AD is
items.answer: For a quadrilateral whose four sides are tangent to a circle, the sums of opposite sides are equal: AB + CD = BC + AD. Substituting, 6 + 4 = 7 + AD, so AD = 10 − 7 = 3 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: Two concentric circles are of radii 10 cm and 8 cm, then the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle is
items.answer: Let the chord AB of the larger circle touch the smaller circle at P. Then OP ⊥ AB and P is the midpoint of AB, with OP = 8 cm and OA = 10 cm. By Pythagoras, AP² = 100 − 64 = 36, so AP = 6 cm and AB = 2AP = 12 cm.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In the given figure, PA is a tangent from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If ∠POB = 115°, then perimeter of ∠APO is
items.answer: The tangent PA is perpendicular to the radius OA, so ∠OAP = 90°. Since AOB is a straight line, ∠AOP = 180° − 115° = 65°. In triangle AOP the angles sum to 180°, so ∠APO = 180° − 90° − 65° = 25°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius
items.ocr: The stem prints 'perimeter of ∠APO'; the options are angles and the solution finds ∠APO = 25°, so this is a misprint for 'measure of ∠APO'. Printed wording kept.

items.stem: From an external point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O. If CD is the tangent to the circle at a point E and PA = 14 cm. The perimeter of ΔPCD is
items.answer: Tangents from an external point are equal, so PA = PB = 14 cm, CA = CE from C and DB = DE from D. The perimeter of ΔPCD is PC + CD + PD = PC + CE + ED + PD = PC + CA + PD + DB = PA + PB = 14 + 14 = 28 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: In the given figure, two tangents AB and AC are drawn to a circle with centre O such that ∠BAC = 120°, then OA is equal to that
items.answer: In triangles OAB and OAC, ∠OBA = ∠OCA = 90° because a radius meets a tangent at right angles, OA is common and OB = OC are radii, so the triangles are congruent by RHS. Hence OA bisects ∠BAC, giving ∠OAB = ½ × 120° = 60°. In right triangle OBA, cos 60° = AB/OA, so ½ = AB/OA and OA = 2AB.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: In the given figure, three circles with centres P, Q and R are drawn, such that the circles with centres Q and R touch each other externally and they touch the circle with centre P, internally. If PQ = 10 cm, PR = 8 cm and QR = 12 cm, then the diameter of the largest circle is:
items.answer: Let the radii be p, q and r. Internal contact gives PQ = p − q = 10 and PR = p − r = 8; external contact gives QR = q + r = 12. Adding the second and third, p + q = 20. Adding this to the first, 2p = 30, so the diameter of the largest circle is 2p = 30 cm.
items.concept: Tangent as one common point

items.stem: If radii of two concentric circles are 4 cm and 5 cm, then the length of each of one circle which is tangent to the other circle, is
items.answer: Let C be the common centre, with r₁ = 4 cm and r₂ = 5 cm, and let AB be the chord of the larger circle touching the smaller circle at P. Then CP ⊥ AB, so in right triangle PAC, AP² = AC² − PC² = 5² − 4² = 25 − 16 = 9, giving AP = 3 cm. The chord AB = 2AP = 6 cm.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius
items.ocr: The stem as printed reads 'the length of each of one circle', with the word 'chord' dropped; the solution finds the length of the chord of the larger circle. Printed wording kept.

items.stem: In figure, if ∠AOB = 125°, then ∠COD is equal to
items.answer: A quadrilateral circumscribing a circle subtends supplementary angles at the centre for opposite sides, so ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°. Hence ∠COD = 180° − 125° = 55°.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: In figure, AT is a tangent to the circle with centre O such that OT = 4 cm and ∠OTA = 30°. Then, AT is equal to
items.answer: Join OA. The tangent AT is perpendicular to the radius OA, so ∠OAT = 90°. In right triangle OAT, cos 30° = AT/OT, so AT/4 = √3/2 and AT = 2√3 cm.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.answer: Both statements are true: the tangents at the two ends of a diameter are each perpendicular to that diameter, so they are parallel to one another, and the diameter is indeed the longest chord. But the length of the chord has nothing to do with why the tangents are parallel, so the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

items.answer: The radii OA and OB are perpendicular to the tangents, so in quadrilateral OAPB, 90° + ∠APB + 90° + 110° = 360°, giving ∠APB = 70°, not 90°. The assertion is therefore false. The reason, that two tangents from an external point are equal in length, is a true statement.
